# Zones and the Wilderness
Some places change what the rules protect. An alert shows the zone you are in, and a line in chat says when you cross in or out. Where you can be attacked (a Wilderness, an outpost at war, or anywhere while you are marked) a banner also shows at the top, with a title and a sound as you cross in. Click the banner to open the rule behind it. Shuttle consoles and mass scanners draw each zone's edge as a dashed ring, except Helios, which keeps its ring off radar as it keeps its IFF.
## Safe Zone [color=#2e9e4f][bold]Green banner.[/bold][/color] Caelestinus Central and everything within 256 m of it. Policy protects everyone here who is not causing trouble: no theft, no unprovoked attacks. See [textlink="Safe Zones" link="MonolithRuleRoleplaySevenSafeZones"].
## Wilderness [color=#d93c3c][bold]Red banner with hazard stripes.[/bold][/color] A PvP zone for everyone: everything within 512 m of an event site: bluespace vaults and weapons caches, wrecks and other bluespace events, planetary vaults and Monolithic Fragments. A salvage wreck someone has claimed is their ship and no longer a Wilderness; claiming a vault, cache or fragment changes nothing. PDV drop pods count as Wildernesses under the rules too, though they show no banner or ring.
While you are being marked, the banner counts down. Once marked, it shows how long your mark, or your ship's, has left, and a faint red border shows round the screen. A marked ship's name shows red with a skull on everyone's radar, and a marked person has a skull over their head. See [textlink="Random deathmatch" link="MonolithRuleConflictOneRandomDeathmatch"].
## Faction outposts [color=#d68c14][bold]Amber banner.[/bold][/color] Within 256 m of a faction outpost such as Halcyon. While the war is COLD, the outpost and ships near it are protected from port strikes; while it is HOT, they may be struck. The banner changes with the war level. See [textlink="Port striking" link="MonolithRuleConflictFourPortStriking"].
## Not a Safe Zone [color=#9aa4ad][bold]Grey banner.[/bold][/color] Aboard, or docked at, a station named as not a Safe Zone, such as Camelot or the Underground Black Market, or a mobile base such as the Jupiter. Ordinary rules and escalation apply.
## Settings Under Options, Wolfgate, Interface, Zones you choose where the banner, the crossing title and the sounds show (in every zone, only where you can be attacked, or never), when the screen border shows, and whether you get the chat lines and the radar rings. The alert always shows, and so do the chat messages about your mark.
